name: Tateyama: Murodo to Mount Oyama (立山 雄山)
region: Chubu-Sangaku National Park, Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route
why: A 3,000 m summit from a bus stop: up a stone path over snowfields to the Ichinokoshi saddle, then a rocky climb to the shrine on top of one of Japan's three sacred mountains.
book: No permit. Reach Murodo by the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route (train, cable car and bus from Toyama, or from the Nagano side): check the timetable and the last bus down. The summit shrine gives a blessing for a fee.
water: Spring water at Murodo terminal (Tamadono spring); drinks at the Ichinokoshi hut. Carry 1 litre.
dangers: Above Ichinokoshi the path is steep loose rock: falling stones, keep distance from walkers above.
Snowfields on the lower path until July: they are slippery in the morning.
Afternoon thunderstorms in summer on a bare ridge: be down from the top by early afternoon.
Cold and wind at 3,000 m even in August: warm layer and shell.
turnaround: Not at Ichinokoshi by 11:30, or clouds building over the ridge: stop at the hut and go back down.

points.name: Murodo terminal
points.note: 2,450 m, where the Alpine Route buses stop. Mikurigaike crater pond is a 10-minute detour north; the Oyama path heads east on stone paving.

points.name: Ichinokoshi
points.note: The saddle at about 2,700 m, with the Ichinokoshi hut: view east over the Kurobe valley to the Ushiro-Tateyama range.

points.name: Oyama shrine summit
points.note: 3,003 m, the Mine-honsha shrine of Oyama jinja on the top. Onanjiyama, 3,015 m, is 20 minutes on along the ridge. Back the same way.
